summary: Cartilage has few but important cells called chondrocytes. The extracellular matrix is firm yet flexible, resilient, and smooth. It gives structure to soft tissues without being rigid. The fibers offer some tensile strength while the ground substance holds water tightly.

text:

• no lymphatic vessels or nerves

summary: Cartilage lacks blood vessels, lymphatic vessels, and nerves. Because of this, chondrocytes must get their nutrients through diffusion from the surrounding matrix. This is why cartilage heals very slowly, or sometimes doesn't heal at all.

summary: There are three types of cartilage. Hyaline cartilage is found in the respiratory tract, joint surfaces, and ribs. Elastic cartilage is in the ear and epiglottis. Fibrocartilage is found in the discs between vertebrae and in the knee meniscus.
